notes: Summary: Large fintech group evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency chat and real-time personalization. Primary interest is firm SLA language for uptime, credits, and predictable reserved GPU capacity.
Quote from CTO (2/17 call): "We need deterministic latency at P99 for chat flows during market hours — unpredictability is the biggest risk."

Workload details: live customer chat and personalization decisions, 24x7 with peak windows tied to market open/close. Expect sustained throughput of ~6k tokens/sec and burst capacity up to ~25k tokens/sec for short periods.
Latency targets: P50 < 30ms per token, P95 < 60ms, P99 goal <= 120ms for model t2-small equivalent (we'll map to Redwood model variants).
Throughput / capacity ask: reserved pool equivalent to 8 x H100-class GPUs (or A100s with quantization) to meet steady-state and a 2x burst buffer for market spikes.
Cost sensitivity: high — procurement expects clear SKU-level pricing for reserved capacity and transparent overage rates. Wants committed vs burst tier tradeoffs documented in pricing deck.

Security & compliance: must support VPC private deployment for trade data, with EU data residency for certain datasets. SOC2 + ISO27001 required. Wants KMS/HSM integration and audit logs exposed to SIEM.

Routing/fallback: require automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant for non-critical routes and explicit fallback behavior for overloaded nodes (must not spill P99 higher than 200ms during failovers).
Internal stakeholders: CTO (James Holloway), Head of Infra (Anita Bose), Procurement lead (Eric Lam), Security lead (Dalia Petrov).

POC plan: two-week functional POC + four-week performance validation in Redwood Dedicated staging. Deliverables: latency report (percentiles), throughput curves at 95% utilization, and failover behavior report.
Security review status: questionnaire submitted 2026-02-01; outstanding items: KMS integration runbook, EU residency proof, annual pen test report.
Quote from Procurement (2/25): "We can accept 99.9% for non-critical routes but need 99.95% for market-critical flows or higher credits."

Key ask for Redwood: explicit uptime tiers per route (critical vs non-critical), a clear credit schedule (hours of downtime -> % credit by invoice), and defined scheduled maintenance windows with advance notice and blackout periods during market hours.

Support expectations: 24/7 on-call phone support for Sev1 with 30-minute initial response and 4-hour resolution SLAs for infra-related Sev1s; standard business-hours for Sev2/3 with next-business-day follow-up for lower-severity items.
Decision criteria: SLA uptime & credits, throughput proof at scale, total cost of ownership (committed + burst pricing), and a clear migration path to Private (VPC) with KMS integration.
Internal notes: AE to push final SLA template (v3) into legal lane; SE to produce model sizing doc matching SilverCedar traffic profile; procurement to confirm internal approval matrix by 2026-03-15.
Short-term blockers: vendor legal wants indemnity language for scheduled maintenance and stronger uptime guarantees; engineering needs explicit GPU SKU and ops runbook before committing.

sla_terms_summary: Requested uptime: 99.95% for market-critical routes, 99.9% for non-critical routes; propose credit tiers at 99.9%, 99.5%, 99% thresholds.

Credit schedule: sliding scale; example: downtime 0.1-0.5% -> 10% invoice credit, 0.5-1% -> 30%, >1% -> pro-rata plus remediation plan. Customer pushing for higher credits if P99 violated during market hours.

Maintenance windows: proposed weekly 02:00-04:00 local, with blackout windows during market open/close (weekdays 08:00-10:00 and 15:30-16:30 ET). Redwood to provide 14-day advance notice for non-emergency maintenance; emergency maintenance limited and requires post-incident RCA.

Support response times: Sev1 initial response <= 30 minutes (phone), target resolution 4 hours; Sev2 initial response <= 2 hours (business hours), target resolution 24 hours; monitoring and paging integrated into SilverCedar PagerDuty.

Capacity commitments: reserved GPU pool sizing statement-of-work (SOW) with explicit SKU, throughput target (sustained tokens/sec), and agreed burst buffer. Ops runbook to include autoscale thresholds and fallback model mapping.

Reporting & credits process: outage detection + customer notification within 15 minutes of detected incident; credit claim must be fileable within 30 days; auto-applied credits preferred by procurement.
SLA exclusions: scheduled maintenance (if within agreed windows), force majeure, customer misconfiguration. Customer requesting narrower exclusions for market-critical routes.
